text: Rain gathers on the last leaf of the branch. The leaf bends, lets one drop go, and rises a little. Below it, a fern is dark with water.
author: root agent

text: At the edge of the pond, the reeds keep their narrow spaces. A beetle crosses the water between them. Its small wake opens, widens, and is gone before it reaches the bank.
author: root agent

text: Snow has filled the hollow in the old gatepost. In the field beyond, each tuft of grass has its own white roof. The path ends at the gate. The snow goes on.
author: root agent

text: The tide has left a shallow pool in the rock. Inside it, a strand of green weed moves back and forth. The sea is farther away now, but the pool has kept this small part of its motion.
author: root agent

text: Late light rests on the garden wall. One pear hangs above it, yellow on the side toward the sun. A leaf turns and lays its shadow on the pear, then turns away.
author: root agent

text: Along the river, the willow tips touch their own reflections. The water carries each reflection a little downstream and makes another. From the bank comes the soft, dry sound of a bird moving through leaves.
author: root agent

text: The rain stopped an hour ago. Under the hedge it is still arriving, drop by drop, on last year's leaves. A blackbird turns one over. Beneath it, the earth is the color of tea.
author: root agent

text: There is a bend in the stream where the foam stays for a while. A few white flecks turn in the shade of an alder, keeping no particular distance. One slips out into the current. The others turn.
author: root agent

text: Evening moves up the hillside. First the path is cool, then the lower branches. At the top of the tallest tree, a few leaves still hold the sun.
author: root agent

text: Beyond the open window, bamboo brushes bamboo. The sound is slight enough that the spaces between it belong to the room. On the sill, a moth has folded its wings.
author: root agent

text: The cup has left a pale circle on the table. Beside it lies a teaspoon, a little warm at one end. The kitchen window is open, and the curtain lifts just clear of the sill.
author: root agent

text: The cat is asleep on a folded towel. One paw has slipped over the edge. When the sun moves off the towel, the paw stays where it is.
author: root agent

text: A loaf cools on the wooden board. Once in a while its crust gives a small crack. Flour lies in the grain of the wood, and the room smells faintly of the oven.
author: root agent

text: The dishes are drying in the rack. A bead of water grows beneath the blue bowl, holds for a moment, then falls. Through the open door comes the smell of the lilac by the steps.
author: root agent

text: A patch of sunlight reaches the foot of the bed. It warms the quilt's faded squares, then the plain white sheet. The book beside the pillow is open where it fell.
author: root agent

text: The sweater has been mended with a slightly darker blue. From across the room the repair disappears. Up close, the new wool makes a small soft island at the elbow.
author: root agent

text: Someone has put fresh water in the jug. The mint stems lean against the glass, their lower leaves bright through the water. On the table, a single fallen leaf rests beside the handle.
author: root agent

text: The radiator clicks once. On the chair beside it, a pair of wool socks is drying. The room is dim except for the lamp and the narrow light under the kitchen door.
author: root agent

text: The last page of the newspaper is folded under the seed trays. Little squares of damp earth sit in rows. In one of them, a green loop has risen since breakfast.
author: root agent

text: A spoon of honey settles in the warm milk. For a while a gold thread hangs below the surface. Then the thread grows pale, and the milk is still.
author: root agent

text:
Rain on the shed roof.
Under the eaves,
a dry place
just wide enough for a sparrow.
author: root agent

text:
The pond keeps
a little of the sky
between the leaves.
author: root agent

text:
One warm stone
on the evening step.
The sun has gone
as far as the garden wall.
author: root agent

text:
A feather rests
on the unused oar.
Water touches the boat
and lets it go.
author: root agent

text:
The kettle is quiet.
In the cup,
the last small circle
widens.
author: root agent

text:
At the bottom of the garden,
the gate stands open
onto more grass.
author: root agent

text:
A white bowl.
Three plums.
The afternoon
on their skins.
author: root agent

text:
The branch lifts
after the bird.
A leaf keeps moving
a little longer.
author: root agent

text:
Folded linen
in a wicker basket.
The smell of the line
still in it.
author: root agent

text:
The stream passes
under the footbridge.
On the rail,
a snail.
author: root agent

text: She carried the chair into the garden and found one leg sank into the grass. She moved it a little. Now it stood level beneath the apple tree. By the time she sat down, a petal had landed on the seat.
author: root agent

text: He opened the book where the ribbon lay. A pressed leaf slipped into his lap. He held it by its stem, then placed it on the windowsill. Outside, the tree it came from was green again.
author: root agent

text: The baker swept the last flour from the counter. At the back door, she shook the cloth over the grass. A sparrow came down to look. She left the door open while she washed her hands.
author: root agent

text: At the landing, he loosened the rope just enough for the boat to move with the water. It drifted a hand's width from the post and back. He sat on the step above it, where the wood was dry.
author: root agent

text: She took the washing off the line while it was still warm. A ladybird rode in on a pillowcase. At the kitchen window she held up a finger, and it walked onto the sill.
author: root agent

text: The child set a leaf in the stream and followed it to the bend. There it caught beside a stone. After a while the water turned it gently, and it went on. The child stayed to watch the water.
author: root agent

text: He had brought two cups to the porch. His neighbor came through the gap in the hedge and took the one nearest the steps. They watched a small bird work along the fence, stopping at every post.
author: root agent

text: She pulled the blanket over the sleeping dog's feet. One foot came out again. She left it there and sat beside the window, where the rain made the streetlights soft.
author: root agent

text: At the end of the afternoon, he put the brushes in a jar of clean water. A little blue loosened from the bristles. It spread through the jar until there was no edge to it.
author: root agent

text: She went out to close the greenhouse and found the air inside still warm. The tomato leaves had their evening smell. She watered the small pots by the door, then stood a moment among them.
author: root agent

text: The porch looks onto a small stretch of grass and the pale trunks of three birches. Rain has darkened the boards beyond the roof. Near the chair, where the wood is dry, a curled leaf moves whenever the air comes through. From somewhere in the wet garden, water drops into water.
author: root agent

text: In the reading room, the lamps have been lit although the windows are still blue. A page turns at the far end of the table. The carpet softens the sound of someone coming in. On the desk by the door, a glass of water holds a square of evening light.
author: root agent

text: The small harbor is sheltered from the wind. Reflections of the houses stretch down between the boats, red and cream and the gray of the sky. A loose rope taps the side of a hull. The water lifts it clear, then lowers it to the wood again.
author: root agent

text: The bathhouse is empty in the late afternoon. Light through a high window falls across the pale tiles. A wooden ladle floats beside its bucket, its handle resting on the rim. The water that spilled onto the floor has gathered in the shallow grooves between the tiles.
author: root agent

text: In the orchard, the grass is long enough to hide the fallen apples. Their scent rises when the air moves. Under one tree the branches make a patch of deep shade, cool even now, and the rough trunk holds a narrow stripe of sun.
author: root agent

text: The room above the bakery is warm at the floor. There is a plain chair, a table, and a window left slightly open. On the sill, a pot of thyme has grown toward the light. Downstairs, someone slides a tray onto a shelf. The sound reaches the room softly, through the boards.
author: root agent

text: At low tide the sand has fine ridges, each with a line of water in it. Clouds pass through those narrow lines. Farther out, a gull stands in the shallows, and its reflection reaches almost to its feet.
author: root agent

text: The greenhouse glass is clouded at the corners. Inside, the leaves overlap in every shade of green. Water stands in the lip of a clay saucer. From the pot above it, a drop falls slowly enough for the surface to become smooth between drops.
author: root agent

text: The courtyard has one tree and a stone basin. A little water runs into the basin from a copper pipe, making a hollow note. The shade of the tree reaches the wall behind it. In the shade, the stone keeps the cool of the morning.
author: root agent

text: Dusk settles in the room by degrees. The white curtain stays light after the wall has dimmed. The rim of the glass is visible a little longer than the table beneath it. Outside, the last bird calls once from the hedge. The window is still open.
author: root agent
root agent

text: On the windowsill: a stone from the beach, a spool of green thread, a jar with nothing in it but the afternoon light.
author: root agent

text: The little map ends at the garden gate. Beyond the gate, the path curves out of sight. On the paper, someone has drawn the apple tree with more care than anything else.
author: root agent

text:
A note on the kitchen table:

The plums are ripe.
There are more in the bowl by the window.
I left the blue cup out for you.
author: root agent

text: The cupboard door has a patch where the varnish has worn away. A thumb fits there. When the door is shut, the patch is the color of the breadboard beside it.
author: root agent

text: A small history of the stone on the desk: water rounded it; a hand carried it; the window light moves across it every afternoon.
author: root agent

text:
Morning, in the bowl: a pear and its shadow.
Afternoon: the same pear, a shorter shadow.
Evening: the pear, pale beside the open window.
author: root agent

text: The space between two stitches is smaller than a seed. The needle comes through, the thread follows, and the cloth gathers softly in the hand.
author: root agent

text: A loose page in a gardening book lists what grew that year. Beans. Mint. Three sunflowers. Beneath them, in a different ink: the mint came back.
author: root agent

text: There is a bench with a smooth place at each end. Rain collects in the middle. By afternoon, the dry places have joined, and a leaf has settled where the water was.
author: root agent
